questions.stem: The NATIONAL ANTHEM of India, 'Jana Gana Mana', was originally written by:
questions.explanation: Jana Gana Mana — composed in Bengali by Tagore (1911), first sung at the INC Calcutta session 27 December 1911. Adopted as national anthem on 24 January 1950. Duration: 52 seconds. Bankim — Vande Mataram (national song). Iqbal — Saare Jahan Se Achha. Bharati — Tamil poet, 'Bharathi'.

questions.stem: The NATIONAL EMBLEM of India is based on the:

options.option_text: Lion Capital of Ashoka at Sarnath

questions.explanation: Sarnath Lion Capital (Ashokan, ~250 BCE) — four Asiatic lions back-to-back on a circular abacus, above a lotus base. Adopted as National Emblem on 26 January 1950. Motto: 'Satyameva Jayate' (Truth alone triumphs) from the Mundaka Upanishad.

questions.stem: The NATIONAL FLAG of India was adopted on:
questions.explanation: Tiranga — adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 22 July 1947, 24 days before independence. Three horizontal bands: saffron (top), white (middle), green (bottom); Ashoka Chakra (24 spokes) in the centre. Designer: Pingali Venkayya. Aspect ratio 2:3.

questions.stem: The Ashoka Chakra in the Indian flag has how many spokes?
questions.explanation: 24 spokes — representing the 24 Dharma Chakra teachings. Navy blue colour. Diameter ≈ 3/4 of the height of the white band.

questions.stem: The NATIONAL CALENDAR of India (Saka era) was adopted on 22 March 1957. Year 1 of the Saka era corresponds to:
questions.explanation: Saka Era — year 1 = 78 CE (begins at Chaitra 1, typically 22 March). Officially adopted 1957 alongside the Gregorian calendar. Used in the Gazette of India. (Vikram Samvat = 57 BCE — used widely in northern India as Hindu calendar.)

questions.stem: Match the NATIONAL SYMBOL with the ITEM. A. National Tree.  B. National Fruit.  C. National River.  D. National Reptile. List-II: 1. Banyan.  2. Mango.  3. Ganga.  4. King cobra.
questions.explanation: Banyan (Ficus benghalensis) — national tree. Mango — national fruit. Ganga — national river (declared 2008). King cobra — national reptile. (Gangetic dolphin = national aquatic animal; tiger = national animal; peafowl = national bird; lotus = national flower.)

questions.stem: The OFFICIAL MOTTO of the Government of India, 'SATYAMEVA JAYATE' ('Truth alone triumphs'), is taken from:
questions.explanation: From the Mundaka Upanishad (3.1.6). Appears below the Ashoka Emblem in Devanagari script. Translation: 'Truth alone triumphs; not falsehood. By truth the divine road is laid out, by which the sages who have fulfilled their desires travel to that supreme abode of truth.'
